items.stem: 3 chairs and 1 table cost ₹900; whereas 5 chairs and 3 tables cost ₹2,100. If the cost of 1 chair is ₹x and the cost of 1 table is ₹y, then the situation can be represented algebraically as
items.answer: Cost of one chair is ₹x and cost of one table is ₹y. 3 chairs and 1 table cost ₹900, thus 3x + y = 900. 5 chairs and 3 tables cost ₹2,100, thus 5x + 3y = 2100. Thus (c) is correct option.

items.section_heading: OBJECTIVE QUESTIONS | Board 2022 Term-1 SQP STD
items.stem: The 2 digit number which becomes 5/6 th of itself when its digits are reversed. The difference in the digits of the number being 1, then the two digits number is
items.answer: If the two digits are x and y, then the number is 10x + y. Now (5/6)(10x + y) = 10y + x. Solving, we get 44x = 55y, so x/y = 5/4. Also x - y = 1. Solving them, we get x = 5 and y = 4. Therefore, the number is 54. Thus (b) is correct option.
items.ocr: MinerU rendered the solution step as '44x + 55y'; the PDF text layer shows the two sides of an equation, so it is written here as 44x = 55y.

items.section_heading: OBJECTIVE QUESTIONS | Board 2022 Term-1 SQP Basic
items.stem: In a number of two digits, unit's digit is twice the tens digit. If 36 be added to the number, the digits are reversed. The number is
items.answer: Let x be the units digit and y the tens digit, then the number is 10y + x. Then x = 2y ...(1). If 36 is added the digits are reversed, i.e. the number becomes 10x + y, so 10y + x + 36 = 10x + y, giving 9x - 9y = 36, i.e. x - y = 4 ...(2). Solving (1) and (2) we have x = 8 and y = 4. Thus the number is 48. Thus (c) is correct option.
items.ocr: Printed number 4 was lost by MinerU; confirmed from the PDF text layer.

items.stem: If (3x + 4y) : (x + 2y) = 9 : 4, then (3x + 5y) : (3x - y) is equal to
items.answer: (3x + 4y)/(x + 2y) = 9/4, hence 12x + 16y = 9x + 18y, or 3x = 2y, i.e. x = (2/3)y. Substituting x = (2/3)y in the required expression we have (3·(2/3)y + 5y)/(3·(2/3)y - y) = 7y/y = 7/1 = 7 : 1. Thus (c) is correct option.

items.stem: A fraction becomes 4 when 1 is added to both the numerator and denominator and it becomes 7 when 1 is subtracted from both the numerator and denominator. The numerator of the given fraction is
items.answer: Let the fraction be x/y. Then (x + 1)/(y + 1) = 4 ⇒ x = 4y + 3 ...(1) and (x - 1)/(y - 1) = 7 ⇒ x = 7y - 6 ...(2). Solving (1) and (2), we have x = 15, y = 3. Thus (d) is correct option.

items.stem: For which value(s) of p, will the lines represented by the following pair of linear equations be parallel: 3x - y - 5 = 0 and 6x - 2y - p = 0
items.answer: Here a₁ = 3, b₁ = -1, c₁ = -5 and a₂ = 6, b₂ = -2, c₂ = -p. Since the given lines are parallel, a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, so (-1)/(-2) ≠ (-5)/(-p), giving p ≠ 5 × 2, i.e. p ≠ 10. Hence p may take all real values except 10. Thus (a) is correct option.
items.ocr: MinerU dropped the two equations out of the stem (they sat on a display line); restored from the PDF text layer. The book prints no 'Thus (x) is correct option' line here - option (a) follows from its own solution p ≠ 10.

items.stem: x and y are 2 different digits. If the sum of the two digit numbers formed by using both the digits is a perfect square, then value of x + y is
items.answer: The numbers that can be formed are xy and yx. Hence (10x + y) + (10y + x) = 11(x + y). If this is a perfect square then x + y = 11. Thus (b) is correct option.
items.ocr: The book prints no 'Thus (x) is correct option' line for this question; the solution ends at x + y = 11, which is option (b).

items.stem: The value of k for which the system of linear equations x + 2y = 3, 5x + ky + 7 = 0 is inconsistent is
items.answer: We have x + 2y - 3 = 0 and 5x + ky + 7 = 0. If the system is inconsistent, then a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂. From the first two ratios, 1/5 = 2/k ⇒ k = 10. Thus (d) is correct option.

items.stem: The value of k for which the system of equations x + y - 4 = 0 and 2x + ky = 3, has no solution, is
items.answer: We have x + y - 4 = 0 and 2x + ky - 3 = 0. Here a₁/a₂ = 1/2, b₁/b₂ = 1/k and c₁/c₂ = (-4)/(-3) = 4/3. Since the system has no solution, a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, so 1/2 = 1/k ≠ 4/3, giving k = 2 and k ≠ 3/4. Thus (d) is correct option.
items.ocr: Option (b) really is printed as the odd value '≠ 2' in the book (the PDF text layer shows the same glyph); kept as printed.

items.stem: The pair of linear equations 2kx + 5y = 7, 6x - 5y = 11 has a unique solution, if
items.answer: Comparing 2kx + 5y - 7 = 0 and 6x - 5y - 11 = 0 with a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0, we get a₁ = 2k, b₁ = 5, c₁ = -7 and a₂ = 6, b₂ = -5, c₂ = -11. For a unique solution a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, so 2k/6 ≠ 5/(-5), i.e. k/3 ≠ -1, hence k ≠ -3. Thus (a) is correct option.
items.ocr: MinerU gave options (b) and (d) as 'k ! 32' and 'k ! 92'; the PDF text layer shows the not-equal sign with the stacked fractions 2/3 and 2/9.

items.stem: The pair of equations x + 2y + 5 = 0 and -3x - 6y + 1 = 0 has
items.answer: Here a₁ = 1, b₁ = 2, c₁ = 5 and a₂ = -3, b₂ = -6, c₂ = 1. Now a₁/a₂ = -1/3, b₁/b₂ = -2/6 = -1/3 and c₁/c₂ = 5/1. We observe that a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, hence the pair of equations has no solution. Thus (d) is correct option.

items.stem: If a pair of linear equations is consistent, then the lines will be
items.answer: Condition for a consistent pair of linear equations: a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂ [intersecting lines having a unique solution] and a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂ [coincident or dependent lines]. So the lines are intersecting or coincident. Thus (c) is correct option.

items.stem: For what value of k, do the equations 3x - y + 8 = 0 and 6x - ky = -16 represent coincident lines?
items.answer: The equations are 3x - y + 8 = 0 and 6x - ky + 16 = 0. Condition for coincident lines is a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂. Here a₁ = 3, b₁ = -1, c₁ = 8 and a₂ = 6, b₂ = -k, c₂ = 16. So 3/6 = (-1)/(-k) = 8/16, giving 1/k = 1/2 [since 3/6 = 8/16 = 1/2], hence k = 2. Thus (c) is correct option.

items.stem: The pair of equations x = a and y = b graphically represents lines which are
items.answer: The pair of equations x = a and y = b graphically represents lines which are intersecting at (a, b). Thus (d) is correct option.

items.stem: If the lines given by 3x + 2ky = 2 and 2x + 5y + 1 = 0 are parallel, then the value of k is
items.answer: We have 3x + 2ky - 2 = 0 and 2x + 5y + 1 = 0. Condition for parallel lines is a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂ ...(i). Here a₁ = 3, b₁ = 2k, c₁ = -2 and a₂ = 2, b₂ = 5, c₂ = 1. From (i), 3/2 = 2k/5 ≠ -2/1. Considering 3/2 = 2k/5 [3/2 ≠ -2/1 in any case], k = 15/4. Thus (c) is correct option.

items.stem: The value of c for which the pair of equations cx - y = 2 and 6x - 2y = 3 will have infinitely many solutions is
items.answer: Condition for infinitely many solutions: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂. Here a₁ = c, b₁ = -1, c₁ = -2 and a₂ = 6, b₂ = -2, c₂ = -3. So c/6 = (-1)/(-2) = (-2)/(-3). From c/6 = 1/2 we get c = 3, and from c/6 = 2/3 we get c = 4. Since c has different values, for no value of c will the pair of equations have infinitely many solutions. Thus (d) is correct option.

items.stem: One equation of a pair of dependent linear equations is -5x + 7y = 2. The second equation can be
items.answer: For dependent linear equations a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂. Option (a): -5/10 ≠ 7/14, rejected. Option (b): -5/(-10) ≠ 7/(-14), rejected. Option (c): -5/(-10) = 7/14 ≠ -2/4, rejected. Option (d): -5/10 = 7/(-14) = -2/4, so it is dependent. Thus (d) is correct option.

items.stem: If x = a and y = b is the solution of the equations x - y = 2 and x + y = 4, then the values of a and b are, respectively
items.answer: Since x = a and y = b is the solution, these values satisfy both equations: a - b = 2 ...(1) and a + b = 4 ...(2). Adding (1) and (2), 2a = 6, so a = 3. Substituting a = 3 in (2), 3 + b = 4 ⇒ b = 1. Thus a = 3 and b = 1. Thus (c) is correct option.

items.stem: Aruna has only ₹1 and ₹2 coins with her. If the total number of coins that she has is 50 and the amount of money with her is ₹75, then the number of ₹1 and ₹2 coins are, respectively
items.answer: Let the number of ₹1 coins be x and the number of ₹2 coins be y. Then x + y = 50 ...(1) and x × 1 + y × 2 = 75, i.e. x + 2y = 75 ...(2). Subtracting (1) from (2): (x + 2y) - (x + y) = 75 - 50, so y = 25. From (2), x = 75 - 2(25) = 25. Thus there are 25 coins of each kind. Thus (d) is correct option.
items.ocr: The rupee sign came through MinerU as a yen sign and as '<' in the text layer; written here as the rupee sign. Equation (1) x + y = 50 was dropped by MinerU and restored from the text layer.

items.stem: The father's age is six times his son's age. Four years hence, the age of the father will be four times his son's age. The present ages (in year) of the son and the father are, respectively
items.answer: Let the present age of the father be x years and of the son be y years. Four years hence, (x + 4) = 4(y + 4), i.e. x - 4y = 12 ...(1). As the father's age is six times the son's age, x = 6y ...(2). Putting (2) in (1): 6y - 4y = 12, so 2y = 12, y = 6. Then x = 6 × 6 = 36. Hence the father is 36 years and the son is 6 years old. Thus (c) is correct option.
items.ocr: MinerU wrote the substitution step as '6x - 4y = 12'; the PDF text layer shows 6y - 4y = 12, corrected here.

items.stem: Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Choose the correct option out of the four given.
items.assertion: Pair of linear equations 9x + 3y + 12 = 0, 18x + 6y + 24 = 0 have infinitely many solutions.
items.reason: Pair of linear equations a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 have infinitely many solutions, if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.

items.answer: From the given equations, 9/18 = 3/6 = 12/24, i.e. each ratio equals 1/2, so a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂ and the pair has infinitely many solutions. Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A). Thus (a) is correct option.
items.ocr: Conflict: the printed assertion reads '8x + 6y + 24 = 0' (MinerU and the PDF text layer agree), but the worked solution computes 9/18 = 3/6 = 12/24 and the key says (a). The solution wins, so the second equation is given here as 18x + 6y + 24 = 0.
